'''Ryoo Ryong''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] (born 1955<ref name="53inNov2008"/>) is a distinguished professor of chemistry at [[KAIST]] in [[Daejeon]], [[South Korea]].<ref name=":chemkaist"/> He was the head of the Center for Nanomaterials and Chemical Reactions, an Extramural Research Center of the [[Institute for Basic Science]]. Ryoo has won a variety of awards, including the [[Top Scientist and Technologist Award of Korea]] given by the South Korean government in 2005. He obtained the KOSEF Science and Technology Award in 2001 for his work on the synthesis and [[crystal structure]] of [[mesoporous silica]].<ref>http://kosef.nextdata.co.kr/index.jsp?filename=C0012/2001_10_A.htm{{dead link|date=April 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

Ryoo obtained his bachelor's degree from [[Seoul National University]] in 1977,<ref name=":chemkaist"/><ref name=cv>[http://rryoo.kaist.ac.kr/professor/professor_sub01.html KAIST: Professor Ryong Ryoo]</ref> his master's from KAIST in 1979,<ref name=":chemkaist"/><ref name=cv/> and his doctorate from [[Stanford University]] in 1986.<ref name=cv/> After completing his master's degree, he worked for three years at the [[Korean Atomic Energy Research Institute]]. After returning to Korea in 1986, he took a position with KAIST.

In 2006, Ryoo and his research team announced the discovery of a form of [[zeolite]] that can catalyze [[petrochemistry|petrochemical]] reactions much more effectively than previous zeolites. Because of the potential of this to streamline the [[gasoline]] refining process, it was greeted as a "magical substance" by the South Korean press.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://times.hankooki.com/lpage/200608/kt2006080710325612070.htm |title= Korean Scientists Create Magical Substance |accessdate=May 14, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060818184414/http://times.hankooki.com/lpage/200608/kt2006080710325612070.htm |archivedate=August 18, 2006 }}</ref>

==Education==
Ryoo graduated Suwon High School, then graduated with a bachelor's degree in applied chemistry from the Seoul National University. He received his PhD in chemistry from Stanford University in 1985 under the supervision of Prof. Michel Boudart.<ref name=":chemkaist">{{cite web |url= https://chem.kaist.ac.kr/research/menu4.php?pmode=view&idx=18 |title= Faculty |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Chemistry Department |publisher= KAIST |access-date= 5 October 2018 |quote=}}</ref> His PhD thesis is ''Platinum Clusters in Y-Zeolite – Studies by Physical and Chemical Probes''. Prior to the PhD course, Ryoo worked at [[Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute]] as a researcher.

==Work==
After obtaining his Ph.D. from Stanford University in 1986, Ryoo worked at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory ([[University of California, Berkeley|U. C. Berkeley]]) as a Postdoctoral Fellow. He studied solid-state NMR under the supervision of Prof. Alex Pines (Jan. 1986 - Nov. 1986). Then he moved to the Department of Chemistry at KAIST as a professor (Dec. 1986).

During his research at KAIST, Ryoo laid scientific cornerstones on nanoporous carbon and hierarchically nanoporous zeolite materials science.  He developed a hard-templating synthesis strategy toward nanoporous carbon material and its application to the research field of fuel cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Ryoo |first1= Ryong |last2= Joo |first2= Sang Hoon |last3= Jun |first3= Shinae |date= 27 August 1999 |title= Synthesis of highly ordered carbon molecular sieves via template-mediated structural transformation |url= https://www.researchgate.net/publication/231665278 |journal= The Journal of Physical Chemistry B |volume= 103 |issue= 37 |pages= 7743–7746 |doi= 10.1021/jp991673a |access-date= 5 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Joo |first1= Sang Hoon |last2= Choi |first2= Seong Jae |last3= Oh |first3= Ilwhan |last4= Kwak |first4= Juhyoun |last5= Liu |first5= Zheng |last6= Terasaki |first6= Osamu |last7= Ryoo |first7=Ryong |date= 12 July 2001 |title= Ordered nanoporous arrays of carbon supporting high dispersions of platinum nanoparticles |url= https://www.researchgate.net/publication/11892865 |journal= Nature |volume= 412 |issue= 6843 |pages= 169–172 |doi= 10.1038/35084046 |pmid= 11449269 |bibcode= 2001Natur.412..169J |s2cid= 4428691 |access-date= 5 October 2018}}</ref> This synthesis strategy is being evaluated as a creative and innovative approach for synthesis of not only nanoporous carbon, but also other nanoporous materials such as zeolites, polymers and metal oxides.

In addition, Ryoo has been focusing on the synthesis of hierarchically nanoporous zeolite materials and their catalytic applications. In this work, he proposed several innovative synthesis strategies in porous materials preparation. He reported the organosilane-directed synthesis route to the mesoporous zeolites.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Choi |first1= Minkee |last2= Cho |first2= Hae Sung |last3= Srivastava |first3= Rajendra |last4= Venkatesan |first4= Chithravel |last5= Choi |first5= Dae-Heung |last6= Ryoo |first6= Ryong |date= 6 August 2006 |title= Amphiphilic organosilane-directed synthesis of crystalline zeolite with tunable mesoporosity |url= http://www.canli.dicp.ac.cn/Articles%20of%20Group%20Seminars/20070127zhanglei.pdf |journal= Nature Materials |volume= 5 |issue= 9 |pages= 718–723 |doi= 10.1038/nmat1705 |pmid= 16892049 |bibcode= 2006NatMa...5..718C |s2cid= 16490891 |access-date= 5 October 2018}}</ref> Ryoo also released an article on the synthesis of single-unit-cell thick nanosheet zeolites.<ref name=":461"/> In this approach, a surfactant chemically incorporating a zeolite structure-directing head group was used, which can generate zeolite micropores as well as mesoporous structures simultaneously in a single synthesis step.

Ryoo received the Breck Award from the International Zeolite Association in 2010. In 2011, he extended the surfactant-directing synthesis strategy to various nanoporous structures such as hexagonal honeycomb and disordered [[Nanosponges|nanosponge]], rather than lamellar-type nanosheet, and reported these results in ''Science'' (2011). In 2007, Ryoo was named [[National Scientist of the Republic of Korea]] and has received research funds as part of the award. In addition, he became a distinguished professor in the Department of Chemistry at KAIST in 2008. He is a fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry, and member of the Editorial Board for both ''Chemical Communications'' and ''ChemCatChem''.
